## Microsoft Gross Margin: FY2023 vs. FY2024

**Comparability note:** Both periods are twelve-month fiscal years ended June 30 and are drawn from the same FY2024 10-K (FY2023 appears as the comparative column), so the accounting basis and fiscal calendar are directly comparable [DOC: msft_margin.txt — Microsoft Corporation 10-K FY2024, accession 0000950170-24-087843]. The filing excerpts available here do not disclose any segment redefinition or divestiture affecting the comparison; note, however, that FY2024 revenue includes a partial year of the Activision Blizzard business acquired during FY2024, which is an organic-vs-inorganic (not an accounting-basis) difference.

### Calculation

| | FY2024 | FY2023 |
|---|---|---|
| Revenue | $245,122M [DOC] | $211,915M [DOC] |
| Cost of revenue | $74,114M [DOC] | $65,863M [DOC] |
| **Gross margin ($)** | **$171,008M** | **$146,052M** |
| **Gross margin (%)** | **69.76%** | **68.92%** |

- FY2024: ($245,122M − $74,114M) ÷ $245,122M = **69.76%**
- FY2023: ($211,915M − $65,863M) ÷ $211,915M = **68.92%**

### Conclusion

Gross margin **improved** by approximately **0.84 percentage points** (roughly 85 basis points). Revenue grew ~15.7% while cost of revenue grew only ~12.5%, meaning revenue outpaced cost growth — gross profit dollars rose $24,956M, from $146,052M to $171,008M (+17.1%).

ANSWER: Improved — gross margin rose from 68.92% in FY2023 to 69.76% in FY2024, an increase of approximately 0.84 percentage points (~85 bps).
